angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 264,366 km at 22.03 pc = 0.16 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 45.3972 +/- 0.0301 mas (same row, RUWE 1.24): 22.03 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.38 +/- 0.012 solar radii from Bonfanti et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of LTT 3780 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A..66B/abstract): 264,366 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.381 +/- 0.024 solar masses from Bonfanti et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of LTT 3780 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A..66B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3358 +/- 92 K from Bonfanti et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LTT 3780 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A..66B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Bonfanti et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of LTT 3780 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A..66B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/ltt-3780.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.859, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 3780 (pscomppars): spectral type M3.5 V, from Weisserman et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...709A.165W/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 3780 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.06 dex, from Bonfanti et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A..66B/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 3780 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -1.78252, from Bonfanti et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A..66B/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 3780 (pscomppars): age 3.1 Gyr, from Bonfanti et al. 2024 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A&A...682A..66B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 3780 (pscomppars): rotation period 104 d, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of LTT 3780 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.3 km/s, from Kokori et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..265....4K/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
